facts.claim: RFC 3629: in UTF-8, the US-ASCII characters (plain English letters, digits and punctuation) take one byte each.
Jacob Ziv and Abraham Lempel published the pointer method now called LZ77 in 1977, in IEEE Transactions on Information Theory.
David Huffman published his method for building minimum-redundancy codes in the Proceedings of the IRE in 1952.
Byte pair encoding, the way many tokenizers build their vocabulary, began as a data compression algorithm (Sennrich, Haddow and Birch, 2016).
RFC 1951: DEFLATE compresses data using a combination of the LZ77 algorithm and Huffman coding, with lengths of 3 to 258 bytes and distances up to 32K bytes.
RFC 1952: a gzip file is DEFLATE data with a 10-byte header and an 8-byte trailer (a CRC-32 check and the original size).
RFC 7932: Brotli also compresses data using a combination of the LZ77 algorithm and Huffman coding.
The Compression Streams standard (updated 19 October 2026) lets a web page compress with brotli, deflate, deflate-raw and gzip.
RFC 1951: no lossless compression algorithm can compress every possible input data set.
Claude Shannon’s 1948 “A Mathematical Theory of Communication” defined entropy, the average bits per symbol no code can beat.
The JPEG committee describes JPEG as a Huffman-coded, DCT-based lossy image format.
